newsitem.title: USA: NTSB probing report that missile flew near jet.
newsitem.headline: NTSB probing report that missile flew near jet.

text.p: The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating a report by an American Airlines pilot that he sighted a missile off the right wing of his 757 as it flew near NASA and Navy facilities last week, a spokesman said on Saturday.
NTSB spokesman Peter Goelz confirmed the investigation, first reported in the daily newspaper Newsday, noting that the pilot took no evasive action and none was needed.
The reported incident took place at 1:45 p.m. (1745 GMT) Aug. 29 as American Airlines flight 1170 flew over Wallops Island, Virginia enroute from San Juan, Puerto Rico, Goelz said.
Wallops Island is home to NASA's sounding rocket program of unmanned research rockets.
"We have sent an investigator to look into a report that he saw a missile off the wing of his plane," Goelz said.
There are two Navy installations near the site of the incident as well -- at Norfolk, Viriginia and in Lexington Park, on the Patuxent River.

Investigators looking into the cause of the July 17 explosion off Long Island of TWA Flight 800, which killed all 230 people aboard, have raised the possibility that the crash may have been caused by a missile, a bomb or mechanical failure.
So far they have remained close-mouthed on any further evidence to support or rule out any of the three theories.
They have found microscopic traces of a chemical explosive on the debris, but say they need further evidence such as physical damage to draw a conclusion.
